title: Qualitative Completeness and Abstract-Operation Audit Policy
purpose: Separate source completeness from parser success so later regression analysis can compare model outputs without hiding abstraction behind canonicalisation.
principles: Explicit procedural logic is preserved as written except for auditable surface/structural canonicalisation.
An explicitly stated abstract operation may be minimally operationalised when later source statements depend on state or results that the abstraction necessarily establishes.
Operationalisation must preserve the abstract operation's position in control flow and may not rewrite later explicit procedural logic.
Task intent is evidence for later correctness analysis and must not override contradictory explicit model procedure during canonicalisation.
Every operationalised abstract instruction must be recorded in the audit so later analysis can measure canonicalisation burden.

recommended_fields.abstract_operations: list of exact or near-exact source operations
recommended_fields.dependency_on_abstract_state: later source expressions that consume the abstraction
